title: Tiny-chunk thrashing under dynamic sequence lengths — allocator fragmentation investigation
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Summary: Intermittent GPU RSS growth and long-tail latency spikes observed on mixed-length streaming workloads. Symptoms appear when many small ephemeral allocations (~256B–8KB) are created by KV cache patches and tokenized micro-batches with dynamic sequence lengths. The hypothesis is allocator internal fragmentation + cudaMallocAsync slab scattering causes thrashing as the stream-affinity heuristics fail to coalesce small frees, leaving many tiny live fragments that prevent larger contiguous allocations during occasional heavy batches.

Steps to reproduce (observed in staging):
- Start continuous streaming workload with heterogeneous sequence lengths (avg 120, tail 2048).
- Enable KV prefetching and per-request small scratch allocations (alignment 64).
- Run for ~10k requests.
- Observe gradual RSS increase on device and growing stddev in allocation latency; spikes occur when a large batch requires a contiguous block.

Evidence collected:
- Allocation histogram (staging profiler): 74% of successful allocations in hot path are <4KB, but large allocations (>32MB) fail intermittently despite free memory reported by cudaMallocAsync.
- cudaMallocAsync call traces show frequent small allocations on different streams without pinned staging reuse.
- nvprof / nsight sampling shows many small resident fragments (fragment-size distribution attached to Confluence link).
- Heap metadata snapshots show slab occupancy spread across ~120 arenas with many single-chunk allocations.

Hypotheses: 
1) Small ephemeral allocations from KV patching are not being aggregated into the allocator's staging pools due to stream affinity mismatches, causing many 64/256/1024B fragments.
2) cudaMallocAsync internal freelists are being returned to the driver in a pattern that prevents coalescing, creating fragmented device-resident pages.
3) Combined effect with continuous batching: merging of batches occasionally produces a demand for a large contiguous allocation which fails or stalls while allocator scavenges, causing end-to-end latency spikes.

Proposed investigation plan: 
- Add allocation-size tracking in the runtime (per-stream histograms) to confirm distribution and cross-stream churn.
- Reproduce locally with unit test harness that simulates KV prefetch allocation pattern and dynamic seq lengths (seeded fuzzer for sequence lengths).
- Instrument cudaMallocAsync call sites with stream tags and allocation IDs to build cross-stream lifetime traces.
- Try mitigations in a branch: a) enforce small-allocation pooling (micro-slabs) with a reuse cache keyed by stream group, b) force async-free drain frequency tuning, c) add lightweight coalescer for staging host-pinned pages.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Reproduction harness shows stable RSS across 50k simulated requests with mixed seq lengths.
- Staging runs demonstrate <10% variance in 95th percentile latency and no unexplained memory growth over 24h.
- A PR implementing pooling + stream-group reuse is reviewed and benchmarked with before/after traces attached.
comments: 2026-02-06 — Liam Chen: Initial spike reported by ops on staging-nyc1. Noticed pattern after KV prefetch roll. Opening ticket and attaching initial profiler output to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/ENG-531210-alloc-frag

2026-02-09 — Asha Patel: Ran lightweight reproducer locally. Confirmed many small allocations create scatter across arenas. Snippet from local run: alloc_count(<4KB)=82341, unique_streams=48, arena_spread=112. Pushing instrumented binary to staging branch 'eng/531210/trace'.

2026-02-14 — Miguel Ortega (review): Looked at trace logs. There are frequent cross-stream frees that end up on different worker threads; cudaMallocAsync's deferred freeing depends on stream synchronization which we don't always trigger. Suggest grouping KV small-allocs by a short-lived worker-local pool to reduce cross-stream returns.

2026-02-20 — Asha Patel: Implemented micro-slab pool (configurable via RUNTIME_MICROS_SLAB=true) and stream-grouping heuristic. Benchmarked on c6g-32g (GPU sim): RSS growth reduced by ~62% in reproducer, p95 latency improved by 18%. Opening draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219

2026-02-25 — Performance team (notes): Need to ensure pool doesn't increase fragmentation for large-allocation workloads. Added test case where >64MB allocation occurs every 500 requests. Micro-slab pool + eviction heuristics pass initial smoke but need extended soak. Added integration job 'allocator-soak-72h'.

2026-03-03 — Ops: Staging soak at 72h shows no ongoing RSS trend but occasional 2–3 second stalls when eviction triggers under burst. Captured stack trace: runtime::evict_to_satisfy(allocator.cpp:872). Possibly lock contention when coalescing. Marked as follow-up to optimize eviction path.

2026-03-08 — Asha Patel: Optimized eviction path to use lock-free try-evict window; preliminary microbenchmarks show stall reduced to 200–400ms. Preparing benchmark artifacts. Will open follow-up ticket for lock-free improvements if this doesn't stabilize in next soak.

2026-03-10 — Jake Morrison (PM): Good progress. Please add a short note in release notes for runtime-1.22 about improved small-allocation pooling and a rollback flag RUNTIME_MICROS_SLAB=false. Target to complete by release cut if soak remains green.
notes: Follow-ups: create ENG-531211 to harden eviction without global locks; ENG-531212 to add CI job that fuzzes seq length distributions. Consider telemetry: expose small-allocation churn metric in Console (opt-in).
